ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The two daily gruel-and-rice meals are the monastery’s fixed meal-times. Zhaozhou says that during forty years he had no mixed use of mind apart from these meals; later masters quote, challenge, and institutionalize that formula, including the right of ordained residents to receive them.
EvidenceBody: Zhaozhou’s saying defines the recurring formula: apart from the two gruel-and-rice meals, he had no mixed use of mind. Lamp and instruction records repeatedly quote it.
Wuzhun Shifan asks where Zhaozhou fell outside the two meals, then counters that when gruel comes one eats gruel and when rice comes one eats rice.
Gaofeng Yuanmiao uses the same phrase autobiographically when saying that for nearly three years he did not mount the cushion outside the two meal-times.

Qianshan Shengren gives the phrase an institutional edge: before ordination, he says, even the two daily meals count as stolen food. The headword names actual scheduled meals before it carries any quoted contrast.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: An ordinary meal schedule becomes a fixed Chan formula for the only interruption in Zhaozhou’s forty-year statement and a publicly regulated monastic entitlement.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase is not a general name for all food or all monastery activity; it specifies two scheduled gruel-and-rice meals.

ComparedThings: Zhaozhou’s exception, Gaofeng’s schedule, Qianshan’s entitlement ruling, and later comments all point to the monastery’s same two scheduled meals
DifferentThingTest.Reason: Zhaozhou’s exception, Gaofeng’s schedule, Qianshan’s entitlement ruling, and later comments all point to the monastery’s same two scheduled meals.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Two, daily, meal-times, gruel, rice, morning, and midday make the schedule searchable without reducing it to generic food.

ModifierControls.reason: 二時 fixes the twice-daily schedule and 粥飯 names gruel and rice together; hits for 粥飯 without 二時 were not counted as the full formula.

FamilyControls.reason: 粥飯, 粥飯僧, and 二時上堂 are neighboring institutional terms. Only 二時粥飯 names the two-meal formula raised from Zhaozhou.
